options.label: Use the Common Era
options.rule: For years, use the Common Era. Example: 1922年.

options.label: Use the Japanese imperial era
options.rule: For years, use the Japanese imperial era. Example: 大正11年.

options.label: Use kanji numbers for approximate numbers
options.rule: Use kanji numbers for approximate numbers. Examples: 二十余人; 数十人; 四、五十人.

options.label: Use kanji numbers for phrases and native counting
options.rule: Use kanji numbers for numbers used in phrases and the counting method based on native Japanese readings in the Standard Kanji Table. Examples: 二者択一; 一つ; 二つ; 一人; 二人; 六法全書; 七五三.

options.label: Add a currency unit in Japanese after the number
options.rule: For currencies, add a currency unit in Japanese after the number. Examples: 100円; 50ドル; 300ユーロ.

options.label: Add a full-width currency unit symbol without a space
options.rule: For currencies, add a full-width currency unit symbol without a space in between. Examples: ￥100; ＄50.

options.label: Add a half-width currency unit symbol without a space
options.rule: For currencies, add a half-width currency unit symbol without a space in between. Examples: ¥100; $50.

options.label: Add a half-width currency unit symbol with a half-width space
options.rule: For currencies, add a half-width currency unit symbol with a half-width space in between. Examples: ¥ 100; $ 50.

options.label: Add a comma every three digits
options.rule: For large numbers other than calendar year numbers, add a comma every three digits. Examples: 5,000; 62,250円; 1,254,372人.

options.label: Use kanji for trillions, hundred millions, and ten thousands
options.rule: For large numbers, use kanji for trillions, hundred millions, and ten thousands. Examples: 5兆; 100億; 30万.

options.label: Use commas and a decimal point
options.rule: For large numbers other than calendar years, add a half-width “,” for every three digits, and a half-width “.” for a decimal point. Example: 5,000.023.

options.label: Use a full-width percent sign without a space
options.rule: For percentages, use a full-width “%” without a space between the number and the symbol. Example: 100％.

options.label: Use katakana
options.rule: For percentages, use katakana (“パーセント”). Example: 100パーセント.

options.label: Use a half-width percent sign with a space
options.rule: For percentages, use a half-width “%” with a space between the number and the symbol. Example: 100 %.

options.label: Spell with katakana or katakana and kanji
options.rule: For metric units, spell with katakana or katakana and kanji. Examples: メートル; メートル毎秒.

options.label: Use unit symbols
options.rule: For metric units, use unit symbols. Examples: m; m/s.

options.label: Use the kanji unit of 度
options.rule: For temperatures, use the kanji unit of “度”. Example: 20度.

options.label: Use ℃ with a space
options.rule: For temperatures, use °C as a unit with a space between the number and the unit. Example: 20 ℃.

options.label: Use ℃ without a space
options.rule: For temperatures, use °C as a unit without a space between the number and the unit. Example: 20℃.

rules.title: Use of hiragana and kanji
rules.rule: When using Arabic numerals in horizontal writing, use “○か所” or “○か月,” but when using kanji numbers, use “○箇所” or “○箇月.” Examples: ３か所; ７か月; 三箇所; 七箇月.

options.label: Use kanji numbers
options.rule: When writing numbers, use kanji numbers.

options.label: Use full-width Arabic numerals
options.rule: When writing numbers, use full-width Arabic numerals and use Kanji numbers only where it would otherwise sound unnatural. Examples: １; ２; ３; 第一歩; 一生.

options.label: Use half-width Arabic numerals
options.rule: When writing numbers, use half-width Arabic numerals and use kanji numbers only where it would otherwise sound unnatural. Examples: 1; 2; 3; 第一歩; 一生.

rules.title: Corner brackets and periods
rules.rule: When inserting a sentence using corner brackets (「...」), follow the preferred Japanese punctuation pattern consistently.

options.label: Use one ellipsis
options.rule: When omitting a part of a sentence or leaving a lingering impression, use one ellipsis (“…”).

options.label: Use three ellipses
options.rule: When omitting a part of a sentence or leaving a lingering impression, use three ellipses (“………”).

options.label: Use two ellipses
options.rule: When omitting a part of a sentence or leaving a lingering impression, use two ellipses (“……” ).

rules.title: Double corner brackets
rules.rule: Use double corner brackets to emphasize words, for reference material written in Japanese, and for nested corner brackets.

rules.title: Round brackets and periods
examples: 今年の生産量は10tだった。（昨年は8tだった。）
rules.rule: When the round brackets enclose a complete sentence, add a Japanese period to that sentence as well. Example: 今年の生産量は10tだった。（昨年は8tだった。）.

rules.title: The text in round brackets modifies the entire sentence

options.label: Add a period after the closing round bracket
examples: 今日は歩いて出かけた（昨日は走って出かけた）。
options.rule: When the text in round brackets modifies the entire sentence, add a period after the closing round bracket. Example: 今日は歩いて出かけた（昨日は走って出かけた）。

options.label: Add a period before the closing round bracket
examples: 今日は歩いて出かけた。（昨日は走って出かけた。）
options.rule: When the text in round brackets modifies the entire sentence, add a period before the closing round bracket. Example: 今日は歩いて出かけた。（昨日は走って出かけた。）.

rules.title: When the text in round brackets supplements the preceding text
examples: 今日は歩いて出かけた（兄と）。
rules.rule: When the text in round brackets supplements the preceding text, add a Japanese period after the closing round bracket. Example: 今日は歩いて出かけた（兄と）。

rules.title: Double dashes
examples: 電車が、静岡——浜松——名古屋と進んでいった
rules.rule: When indicating the passage of time or movement between locations, use a double em dash. Examples: 5分——10分——15分; 電車が、静岡——浜松——名古屋と進んでいった.

options.label: Use full-width 。 and 、
options.rule: Use full-width “。” and full-width “、”.

options.label: Use full-width 。 and ，
options.rule: Use full-width “。” and full-width “,”.

options.label: Use full-width ． and 、
options.rule: Use full-width “.” and full-width “、”.

options.label: Use full-width ． and ，
options.rule: Use full-width “.” and full-width “,”.

options.label: Use a full-width dash
options.rule: To indicate a range, use a full-width dash (ー).

options.label: Use a full-width wave dash
options.rule: To indicate a range, use a full-width wave dash (〜).

options.label: Use a half-width dash
options.rule: To indicate a range, use a half-width dash (-).

options.label: Use から
options.rule: To indicate a range, use “から”.

options.label: Use full-width round brackets
options.rule: Use full-width round brackets. Example: データ通信（送信のみ）.

options.label: Use half-width round brackets
options.rule: Use half-width round brackets. Example: データ通信(送信のみ).

options.label: Use full-width quotation marks
options.rule: To indicate a set-off phrase other than a quote, use full-width quotation marks.

options.label: Use half-width quotation marks
options.rule: To indicate a set-off phrase other than a quote, use half-width quotation marks.

options.label: Use the active voice with the user as the subject
examples: サイドパネルのボタンをクリックする
options.rule: When describing operation, use the active voice with the user as the subject to unify the viewpoint. Example: サイドパネルのボタンをクリックする.

options.label: Use the passive voice for automatic operations
options.rule: When operations are automatically performed from the user’s point of view, use the passive voice. Example: データが送信される.

options.label: Use the dearu style
options.rule: Use the “dearu” style when you want to give the impression that the content is accurate and rigorous, or when you want to convey a sense of confidence and reliability.

options.label: Use the desu/masu style
options.rule: Use the “desu/masu” style when you want to give the impression that the content is plain and straightforward, or when you want to give the reader a reassuring or soft impression.

rules.title: Abbreviations
examples: クオリティー・オブ・ライフ（Quality of Life 。 以下「ＱＯＬ」という。）
rules.rule: Write the original term, then add its abbreviation and, where necessary, add an explanation. Example: クオリティー・オブ・ライフ（Quality of Life 。 以下「ＱＯＬ」という。）.

options.label: Add an explanation if plain-language rephrasing is difficult
examples: インクルージョン（多様性を受容し互いに作用し合う共生社会を目指す考え）
多様な人々を受け入れ共に関わって生きる社会を目指す「インクルージョン」は…
options.rule: For loanwords, if it is difficult to rephrase in plain language, add an explanation. Examples: インクルージョン（多様性を受容し互いに作用し合う共生社会を目指す考え）; 多様な人々を受け入れ共に関わって生きる社会を目指す「インクルージョン」は….

options.label: Rephrase with daily-use Chinese or Japanese words
examples: インキュベーション → 起業支援
インタラクティブ → 双方向的
サプライヤー → 仕入先
options.rule: For loanwords, if it can be rephrased in daily-use Chinese or Japanese words, rephrase it. Examples: アジェンダ → 議題; インキュベーション → 起業支援; インタラクティブ → 双方向的; サプライヤー → 仕入先; 供給業者.

options.label: Rephrase with another expression if not established in Japanese
examples: リスクを取る → あえて困難な道を行く
options.rule: For loanwords, if it is not yet established in Japanese, rephrase it with another expression. Examples: リスクを取る → あえて困難な道を行く; 覚悟を決めて進む; 賭ける.

options.label: Use it as is if it is well established in Japanese
options.rule: For loanwords, if it is well established in Japanese, use it as is. Examples: ストレス; ボランティア; リサイクル.
